frame: Wren wrote about her first night aboard the Soggy Biscuit. The Whiskrel slept through all of it.
text:
My first night aboard the Soggy Biscuit was not what I had imagined. I had pictured myself drifting off to sleep under the stars, rocked gently by the tide, dreaming about the Creatures we would rescue. Instead, Tully pointed me to a narrow bunk below deck, squeezed between a cupboard full of tins and a pile of Gus's experiments, and switched off the only light.

I lay there in the pitch dark with my eyes shut, trying not to think about what might be in the experiments. That was when the boat began to talk. The groan of the old hull timbers and the slap of loose rope against the mast kept me awake for hours. Somewhere near my feet, water gurgled through a pipe. Above me, footsteps creaked across the deck as someone on watch walked from one end to the other and back again. Every few minutes, Mo, in the next bunk, let out a snore like a small motorbike starting up.

At some point I must have fallen asleep, because the next thing I knew, sunlight was pouring through the porthole and Mo was offering me a fried egg on a slice of toast that was, somehow, also wet. I said yes. By the third night, I could sleep through anything.

frame: Wren sneaked into Maxx's Green Screen Swamp and wrote down everything she noticed.
text: Notes from inside Green Screen Swamp, 11.40 pm. The door was unlocked, which is typical of Maxx. Inside, it isn't a swamp at all. It's a huge shed, and almost every surface is painted the same flat, glowing green so that Maxx can add fake backgrounds later. Gold spotlights blaze down on a plastic waterfall that pours the same water round and round in a loop. As I creep past it, I can feel cold spray on the back of my neck. Fans whirr everywhere, and a generator in the corner thuds like a giant heartbeat. Somewhere above me, a robot camera gives a little buzz every few seconds. The air reeks of hot plastic and hairspray, which I think is mostly Maxx. A sour whiff of old fish food drifts out from behind the waterfall. Behind the waterfall, I found what we came for: rows of tiny cages stacked against the back wall. When I pressed my palms against the bars of the nearest one, they were cold and greasy, as if nobody had cleaned them in months. A Creature inside blinked at me. I took photos of everything, then crept out before the spotlights could swing my way.

frame: Tully wrote up a famous food critic's review of Mo's Mangrove Cafe. One word in her summary is wrong.
text:
MO'S MANGROVE CAFE: A REVIEW. I have eaten at restaurants on every island in the archipelago, but none of them prepared me for Mo's Mangrove Cafe, a wobbly wooden hut perched on the end of the jetty. I arrived just after sunset. Strings of fairy lights hung over the tables, and the menu was written in chalk on an old surfboard.

I ordered the house special, a mud crab curry. While I waited, I could hear it before I could see it: the curry spat and bubbled in a huge pot behind the counter, and every few seconds something went pop. When it arrived, the first spoonful tasted rich and nutty, then salty, then, strangely, a little bit sweet, as if somebody had stirred in a spoonful of jam. I asked Mo about this. He said it was 'a family secret', and then admitted that it was jam.

For dessert, I tried the sticky date pudding. The bowl was so hot that it warmed my hands right through, which was welcome, because the wind off the water was cold. I would not call the meal perfect, but I would call it unforgettable, and I am already planning to return, although perhaps not for the curry.

frame: Zed found this story in the Mirage Mangroves library. The Whiskrel read it from under a blanket.
text:
Nobody had been inside the old fishing shed at the end of the creek for years. From the outside, it looked like it might fall down if someone sneezed. The tin walls were orange with rust, the windows were boarded up, and a crooked sign on the door said KEEP OUT in faded red paint. Jas and her cousin Theo had dared each other all summer, and on the last night of the holidays, they finally squeezed through the gap in the door with one torch between them.

They had only taken five steps when the torch flickered and died. Theo shook it. Nothing. In the total darkness, the shed seemed to wake up. Something dripped steadily, plink, plink, plink, somewhere above their heads. The tin roof ticked and popped as it cooled. Behind them, the door creaked slowly shut. Then, from the far corner, came a scratching sound, followed by a soft, wet shuffle, as if something heavy was dragging itself across the floor towards them. Jas grabbed Theo's sleeve. Neither of them breathed.

Then Theo's phone lit up with a message from his mum, and in its blue glow they saw a very large, very startled pelican waddling across the floor towards them, dragging an old fishing net behind it. The pelican looked at them. They looked at the pelican. All three of them left the shed at the same time.

frame: Indi wrote a review of the outdoor concert at the mangrove amphitheatre.
text:
The Mangrove Moonlight Concert has been running for twelve years, and this year it was the biggest yet, with more than a thousand people squeezed onto the grassy slope of the amphitheatre. The headline act was a five-piece band from the mainland called The Fiddler Crabs, and by the time they walked on stage, the crowd had been waiting for over an hour in the steamy evening heat.

The moment they started, purple and blue lights swept across the crowd, catching the raised arms and the bubbles drifting up from the front row. The drummer's sticks cracked against the snare like a whip, and the singer's voice soared over the top of it all. Halfway through the second song, a light rain began to fall, but nobody moved. Sweat ran down the back of my neck in the sticky heat. People stood on the hill singing every word. The smell of popcorn and wet grass drifted up from the stalls behind us.

The band played for nearly two hours and finished with an encore that had the whole hill jumping. Walking back to the ferry afterwards, my ears still buzzing and my shirt soaked through, I decided it was the best concert I have ever been to.
